h: Shabbos and Shemittah Nourish Faith in Divine Providence

p: is granted the requests of his heart,
and He will grant you the requests of your heart.'
This delight — I do not know what it is;
'And you shall call Shabbos a delight,'
you must say this is the delight of Shabbos"
And just before it is written (Tehillim 37:3):
dwell in the land and nourish faith";
And since the Gemara sets the verse "And delight"
as speaking of the delight of Shabbos,
it follows that the verse preceding it
of one who delights in Shabbos;
and what connection does it have to Shabbos?
אַךְ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ קי, ב)
But in the holy Zohar (on this parshah, III 110b):
"'And if you say, what shall we eat' (Vayikra 25:20)
which is the purpose of heaven and earth,
for this was the intent of Creation:
that they recognize the power of His kingship;
and this is on the day of Shabbos,
sets aside its affairs for the honor of Heaven.
He ascended and sat upon His Throne of Glory,"
in the manner of what they said
"'Your throne is established from of old' (Tehillim 93:2)
even though You are from eternity,
until Your children sang the Song, etc.";
that is, they recognized the power of His kingship,
"It is they who first made Me King at the Sea
'Hashem shall reign forever and ever,' etc."
And then His kingship became settled,
"What is the difference between a king, etc.,
He sat upon His Throne of Glory.
So too Shemittah in Eretz Yisrael,
where most of their affairs were
and Yisrael set aside an entire year
recognizing that the earth is Hashem's.
And as stated (beginning of Vayikra Rabbah, 1:1):
"'Mighty in strength, who do His word'
of those who keep the seventh year
And this one sees his field lying fallow,
and pays the land tax and is silent;
יֵשׁ לָךְ גִּבּוֹר גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה כּוּלֵּי
is there a greater hero than this? etc."
for it comes from trust in Hashem,
"And if you say, what shall we eat, etc.,
then I will command My blessing, etc."
So too regarding Shabbos is written
a seventh part of the year,
and Yisrael set aside all their affairs
and this comes from their trust in Hashem,

p: as it were, you shall make them, etc."
This is according to what is written
"As it were, as though he made Him above;
the Holy One, blessed be He, said:
and therefore 'and you shall do them'
'and you shall make yourselves' is written, etc."
"as if he made them," regarding words of Torah, etc.
וְעַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב ס, א)
And according to what is written (Zohar II 60a):
that the Holy One, blessed be He,
other than the Holy One, blessed be He, etc.
and 'good' is none other than the tzaddik,
'Say of the tzaddik that he is good.'"
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב
"And God saw the light, that it was good";
and it says in the Gemara
(end of the first chapter of Taanis, 15a):
one merits the shining of the primordial light
'and Your faithfulness in the nights,' etc."
(בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רל, א, בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא)
"He is truth and she is faith."
corresponds to the middah of Malchus:
in the midst of the Children of Yisrael" (Bamidbar 35:34).
it says in the holy Zohar (III 108a):
Yovel is the supernal Mother, etc."
So too it is called in the holy Zohar
and this is the lower Shabbos."
And this is what is written in Rashi's commentary,
as is said of the Shabbos of Creation."
are for the sake of Hashem,
and the Holy One, blessed be He, has
just as I rested on it"
that is, the meals of Shabbos
into the hearts of the Children of Yisrael,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פח, א)
and on the Field of Apples, etc."
when they recognize that everything is Hashem Yisbarach's.
So too at the onset of Shabbos one says,
for he recognizes that Hashem Yisbarach
and this is "Trust in Hashem, etc.
So too the song for Sunday,
"The earth is Hashem's, and its fullness" (Tehillim 24:1),
they recognize that the earth is Hashem's,
So too regarding Shemittah it is written,
"Six years you shall sow your field":
for according to what the intent will be
in the work of the six years,
so will be the holiness of the Shemittah.
for it is a positive mitzvah for the Great Beis Din
that it is such-and-such a year
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר הַמִּצְוֹת לְהָרַמְבַּ״ם זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה)
(as stated in the Rambam's Sefer HaMitzvos, of blessed memory, positive mitzvah 140),
as in the counting of the Omer,
where it is a mitzvah to count the days
and a mitzvah to count the weeks
For the closer it is to Shemittah,
and so too with each cycle
and so too with each and every year,
So too in eating the produce of the seventh year
as in the eating of Shabbos
